summary: Nora's on-demand Google/HK-gov reverse-geocode result now persists in a new `geocode_cache` table instead of a 512-entry in-memory dict that a restart threw away — same lazy, question-triggered cost posture as before, just no longer wasted. `nora.analytics`'s derived home/work places (`presence_derived_places.label`) are now labelled from this cache, read-only — the presence collector and the analytics service still never call a geocoder themselves; a place nobody has asked `where_is` about simply stays unlabelled.
details: New table `geocode_cache` (migration 0016), owned by Nora, keyed on the same ~11m rounding `where_is`'s existing memo cache already used.
`GeocodeCacheStore` port with SQL and fake implementations, contract-tested.
limitations: Lazy fill only — most derived places stay unlabelled until a real `where_is` question resolves that location at least once; there is no proactive backfill.
